name: Cha ca
summary: Tuna cake from Cổng thông tin điện tử tỉnh Bình Định. The same office says a good cake is also the ingredient in bún chả cá. Fried, it is chewy and crisp. Steamed, it carries a thin yellow egg layer.
origin: Quy Nhon. The provincial portal addresses the cake to the city and says the broth of the noodle bowl is tuna bone and head.
texture: The provincial portal says the fried cake is smooth, soft, and chewy without being too fatty, and the steamed cake is the plainer of the two.
taste: It names pepper heat, the sweetness of the fish, and a clear broth scented with grilled shallot and rock sugar. It also describes a broth with bamboo shoot and straw mushroom. Báo Người Lao Động, on the bowl, says the cake has no dill. The cake page adds scallion and dill. Both stay.
howToEat: Eat the steamed cake hot with the chili sauce and a few herb leaves, or order it inside bún chả cá.
The hour is Check on arrival.
where: The provincial portal gives the city and no street. Nguyễn Huệ is the street on the 3 Apr 2019 bowl article.
seoTitle: Cha ca — Quy Nhon tuna cake
seoDescription: Quy Nhon chả cá is a tuna cake, fried or steamed with a thin egg layer, and the cake inside bún chả cá. Dill is in one account and absent in another. Check on arrival.
